title: Insert Interval
keyIdea: The list is sorted and disjoint, so it splits into three runs: intervals that end before newInterval starts (copy), intervals that overlap it (merge into newInterval), and the rest (copy). No sort needed.

approaches.name: Three phases
approaches.idea: Your code: while end < new start → copy; while start ≤ new end → merge into newInterval; push newInterval; copy the rest.
approaches.why: One pass, each interval looked at once; the result holds up to n + 1 intervals.

quiz.q: Which test puts an interval in the first (copy-before) phase?
options: intervals[i][1] < newInterval[0]: it ends before newInterval starts

quiz.q: In the overlap phase, why is the condition intervals[i][0] <= newInterval[1]?
options: Phase 1 already removed everything ending too early, so starting by newInterval's end means overlap

quiz.q: Why is this O(n) while Merge Intervals is O(n log n)?
options: The input is already sorted, so no sort is needed

steps: Is the list sorted and non-overlapping? Can it be empty?
Brute force: append, sort, run Merge Intervals. Cost?
"Sorted disjoint list + one new interval" → which three groups?
